e: Adonoy spoke
to Moshe and Aharon, saying.

h: דַּבֵּ֣ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִקְח֣וּ אֵלֶיךָ֩ פָרָ֨ה אֲדֻמָּ֜ה תְּמִימָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵֽין־בָּהּ֙ מ֔וּם
t: מַלֵּל עִם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסְּבוּן לָךְ תּוֹרְתָא סִמּוּקְתָּא שְׁלֶמְתָּא דִּי לֵית בָּהּ מוּמָא
e: This is the statute of the Torah
which Adonoy commanded, saying;
speak to Bnei Yisroel that they shall take to you a red, perfect cow without a blemish,
upon which no yoke was laid.
Give it
to Elozor the kohein;
he shall take it outside the camp,
and someone shall slaughter it in his presence.

h: וְהִזָּ֞ה אֶל־נֹ֨כַח פְּנֵ֧י אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֛ד מִדָּמָ֖הּ שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים׃
t: וְיַדִּי לָקֳבֵל אַפֵּי מַשְׁכַּן זִמְנָא מִדְּמַהּ שְׁבַע זִמְנִין:
e: Elozor the kohein shall take some of its blood with his finger
and sprinkle it directly facing the Tent of Meeting, some of its blood seven times.

t: יָת מַשְׁכַּהּ וְיָת בִּשְׂרַהּ וְיָת דְּמַהּ
e: Someone shall burn the cow in his presence;
its skin, flesh, blood,
with its waste (that are in its intestines) shall be burned.

h: וְלָקַ֣ח הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עֵ֥ץ אֶ֛רֶז וְאֵז֖וֹב וּשְׁנִ֣י תוֹלָ֑עַת
t: וְיִסַּב כַּהֲנָא אָעָא דְאַרְזָא וְאֵזוֹבָא וּצְבַע זְהוֹרִי
e: The kohein shall take a piece of cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson wool,
and throw them into the burning of the cow.

h: וְכִבֶּ֨ס בְּגָדָ֜יו הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְרָחַ֤ץ בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ בַּמַּ֔יִם
t: וִיצַבַּע לְבוּשׁוֹהִי כַּהֲנָא וְיַסְחֵי בִשְׂרֵיהּ בְּמַיָּא
e: Then the kohein shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water,
and afterwards he may enter the camp;
[however,] the kohein shall be impure until the evening.
Also, the one who burns it
must wash his garments
and bathe his body in water;
he shall remain unclean until the evening.

h: וְאָסַ֣ף אִ֣ישׁ טָה֗וֹר אֵ֚ת אֵ֣פֶר הַפָּרָ֔ה
וְ֠הָיְתָה לַעֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל לְמִשְׁמֶ֛רֶת לְמֵ֥י נִדָּ֖ה חַטָּ֥את הִֽוא׃
t: וְיִכְנוֹשׁ גְּבַר דְּכֵי יָת קִטְמָא דְתוֹרְתָא
וּתְהֵי לִכְנִשְׁתָּא דִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַטָּרָא לְמֵי אַדָּיוּתָא חַטָּאתָא הִיא:
e: A ritually clean person shall gather the cow’s ashes
and place [it] outside the camp in a clean place;
it shall remain a keepsake for the community of Bnei Yisroel for sprinkling water for purification.

h: וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּ֛ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְחֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃
t: וִיצַבַּע דְּכַנֵּישׁ יָת קִטְמָא דְתוֹרְתָא יָת לְבוּשׁוֹהִי
וּתְהֵי לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְגִיּוֹרַיָּא דְּיִתְגַיְּרוּן בֵּינֵיהוֹן לִקְיַם עֳלָם:
e: The one who gathers the cow’s ashes shall wash his garments,
and remain unclean until the evening;
it shall be for Bnei Yisroel and for the proselyte who lives among them an eternal statute.
One who touches the corpse of any [human] soul
shall become unclean for seven days.

h: ה֣וּא יִתְחַטָּא־ב֞וֹ בַּיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י יִטְהָ֑ר
וְאִם־לֹ֨א יִתְחַטָּ֜א בַּיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י לֹ֥א יִטְהָֽר׃
t: הוּא יַדֵּי עֲלוֹהִי בְּיוֹמָא תְלִיתָאָה וּבְיוֹמָא שְׁבִיעָאָה יִדְכֵּי
וְאִם לָא יַדֵּי עֲלוֹהִי בְּיוֹמָא תְלִיתָאָה וּבְיוֹמָא שְׁבִיעָאָה לָא יִדְכֵּי:
e: He shall cleanse himself [be sprinked] with it on the third day and on the seventh day, so that he may become clean;
if he does not have himself cleansed [be sprinked] on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not become clean.

h: כָּֽל־הַנֹּגֵ֡עַ בְּמֵ֣ת בְּנֶפֶשׁ֩ הָאָדָ֨ם אֲשֶׁר־יָמ֜וּת וְלֹ֣א יִתְחַטָּ֗א אֶת־מִשְׁכַּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ טִמֵּ֔א
כִּי֩ מֵ֨י נִדָּ֜ה לֹא־זֹרַ֤ק עָלָיו֙ טָמֵ֣א יִהְיֶ֔ה
t: כָּל דְּיִקְרַב בְּמִיתָא בְנַפְשָׁא דֶאֱנָשָׁא דִי יְמוּת וְלָא יַדֵּי עֲלוֹהִי יָת מַשְׁכְּנָא דַיְיָ סָאָב
אֲרֵי מֵי אַדָּיוּתָא לָא אִזְדְּרִיקוּ עֲלוֹהִי מְסָאָב יְהֵי
e: Whoever touches a corpse of a [human] soul, who died and does not have himself cleansed [be sprinked] defiles the Mishkan of Adonoy (if he enters it),
that soul will be cut off from Yisroel;
because the sprinkling water was not sprinkled on him, he will be impure
his impurity remains.

t: כָּל דְּעָלֵל לְמַשְׁכְּנָא וְכָל דִּי בְּמַשְׁכְּנָא
e: This is the law
[regarding] a person who dies in a tent;
anyone who enters the tent and everything that is in the tent
shall be unclean for seven days.
Any open [earthenware] utensil
that has no cover fastened to it,
shall be unclean.

h: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּ֜ע עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה בַּֽחֲלַל־חֶ֙רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְמֵ֔ת
t: וְכֹל דִּי יִקְרַב עַל אַפֵּי חַקְלָא בִּקְטֵל חַרְבָּא אוֹ בְמֵתָא
e: Anyone who touches, in an open field, one slain by the sword, a corpse,
human bone, or grave,
shall be unclean for seven days.
They shall take for the unclean person
of the ashes from the burnt purification-offering
and he shall place upon them living [spring] water in a vessel.

h: וְלָקַ֨ח אֵז֜וֹב וְטָבַ֣ל בַּמַּיִם֮ אִ֣ישׁ טָהוֹר֒
t: וְיִסַּב אֵזוֹבָא וְיִטְבּוֹל בְּמַיָּא גְּבַר דְּכֵי
וְיַדֵּי עַל מַשְׁכְּנָא וְעַל כָּל מָנַיָּא
e: He shall take hyssop and dip it into the water; [this is done by] a ritually clean person,
he shall sprinkle it on the tent, on all the utensils
and people that were there,
and on anyone who touched the bone,
murder victim, corpse, or grave.

h: וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָהֵ֥ר בָּעָֽרֶב׃
t: וִיצַבַּע לְבוּשׁוֹהִי וְיַסְחֵי בְמַיָּא וְיִדְכֵּי בְרַמְשָׁא:
e: The ritually clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean person
on the third day and on the seventh day;
he shall purify him on the seventh day
when he must wash his garments and bathe in water, and then he becomes clean in the evening.

h: כִּי֩ אֶת־מִקְדַּ֨שׁ יְהוָ֜ה טִמֵּ֗א מֵ֥י נִדָּ֛ה לֹא־זֹרַ֥ק עָלָ֖יו טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃
t: אֲרֵי יָת מַקְדְּשָׁא דַיְיָ סָאִיב מֵי אַדָּיוּתָא לָא אִזְדְּרִיקוּ עֲלוֹהִי מְסָאָב הוּא:
e: A person who became ritually unclean [and enters the Sanctuary] without purifying himself [being sprinkled],
that soul [person] will be cut off from the community;
for he defiled the Sanctuary of Adonoy, the sprinkling water was not sprinkled upon him, he remains unclean.
This shall be the statute for all times;
one who sprinkles the sprinkling waters shall wash his garments,
and one who touches the sprinkling waters
shall remain unclean until the evening.

t: וְכֹל דִּי יִקְרַב בֵּיהּ מְסָאָבָא יְהֵי מְסָאָב
וֶאֱנַשׁ דְּיִקְרַב בֵּיהּ יְהֵי מְסָאָב עַד רַמְשָׁא:
e: Anything which the unclean person touches, shall become unclean;
and anyone touching him shall be ritually unclean until the evening.

h: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּל־הָ֨עֵדָ֤ה מִדְבַּר־צִן֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן
t: וַאֲתוֹ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּל כְּנִשְׁתָּא לְמַדְבְּרָא דְצִין בְּיַרְחָא קַדְמָאָה
e: The entire community of Bnei Yisroel came to the wilderness of Tzin, in the first month.
The people settled in Kodeish [Rekom],
and Miriam died
and was buried there.
There was no water for the community,
and they assembled against Moshe and Aharon.

h: וְל֥וּ גָוַ֛עְנוּ בִּגְוַ֥ע אַחֵ֖ינוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
t: וּלְוֵי דְמִתְנָא בְּמוֹתָא דְאַחָנָא קֳדָם יְיָ:
e: The people quarreled with Moshe
and said,
“Would that we had died by our brothers’ death before Adonoy.
Why did you bring the congregation of Adonoy
into this wilderness
for us and our livestock to die there?

h: לֹ֣א מְק֣וֹם זֶ֗רַע וּתְאֵנָ֤ה וְגֶ֙פֶן֙ וְרִמּ֔וֹן
t: לָא אָתַר כְּשַׁר לְבֵית זְרַע וְאַף לָא תֵינִין וְגוּפְנִין וְרִמּוֹנִין
e: Why did you take us out of Egypt
and bring us
to this terrible place?
It is not a place [fit] for seed, [nor for] figs, grapes, or pomegranates;
and there is no water to drink!”

h: וַיָּבֹא֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן מִפְּנֵ֣י הַקָּהָ֗ל אֶל־פֶּ֙תַח֙ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד
t: וְעַל משֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן מִן קֳדָם קְהָלָא לִתְרַע מַשְׁכַּן זִמְנָא
e: Moshe and Aharon moved away from the assembly to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
and fell on their faces;
the glory of Adonoy appeared to them.
Adonoy spoke to Moshe, saying.

h: קַ֣ח אֶת־הַמַּטֶּ֗ה וְהַקְהֵ֤ל אֶת־הָעֵדָה֙ אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ
t: סַב יָת חוּטְרָא וְאַכְנֵשׁ יָת כְּנִשְׁתָּא אַתְּ וְאַהֲרֹן אָחוּךְ
וּתְמַלְּלוּן עִם כֵּיפָא לְעֵינֵיהוֹן וְיִתֵּן מוֹהִי
e: “Take the staff and assemble the community, you and Aharon your brother,
and speak to the rock in their presence that it may give forth its water;
you will then bring forth for them water from the rock,
and give drink [to] the community and their livestock.”

t: וּנְסִיב משֶׁה יָת חוּטְרָא מִן קֳדָם יְיָ
e: Moshe took the staff from before Adonoy,
as He instructed him.

h: וַיַּקְהִ֜לוּ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־הַקָּהָ֖ל אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַסָּ֑לַע
t: וְאַכְנִישׁוּ משֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן יָת קְהָלָא לָקֳדָם כֵּיפָא
הֲמִן כֵּיפָא הָדֵין נַפֵּק לְכוֹן מַיָּא:
e: Moshe and Aharon assembled the community before the rock;
[Moshe] said to them, “Listen, you rebels!
Can we extract water from this rock for you?”

h: וַיָּ֨רֶם מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־יָד֗וֹ וַיַּ֧ךְ אֶת־הַסֶּ֛לַע בְּמַטֵּ֖הוּ פַּעֲמָ֑יִם
t: וַאֲרֵם משֶׁה יָת יְדֵיהּ וּמְחָא יָת כֵּיפָא בְּחוּטְרֵיהּ תַּרְתֵּין זִמְנִין
e: And Moshe raised his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice;
water rushed out abundantly,
and the community and their livestock drank.

t: בְּכֵן לָא תַעֲלוּן יָת קְהָלָא הָדֵין
e: Adonoy said to Moshe and Aharon,
“Because you did not believe in Me [My word]
to sanctify Me in the presence of Bnei Yisroel;
therefore, you will not bring this congregation
into the land that I have given them.”
They are the waters of dispute
where Bnei Yisroel contended with [before] Adonoy,
and He was sanctified through them.

h: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֧ה מַלְאָכִ֛ים מִקָּדֵ֖שׁ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם
t: וּשְׁלַח משֶׁה אִזְגַּדִּין מֵרְקָם לְוָת מַלְכָּא דֶאֱדוֹם
e: Moshe sent emissaries from Kodeish [Rekom] to the King of Edom (saying),
“This is what your brother Yisroel declares;
you know
of all the hardship that we have encountered.
Our forefathers went down to Egypt
and we remained in Egypt for a long time;
the Egyptians mistreated us and our forefathers.
Then we cried out [prayed] to Adonoy, and He heard our voice [accept our prayer],
He sent an emissary
and led us out of Egypt;
now we are in Kodeish [Rekom],
a city at the edge of your border.

h: נַעְבְּרָה־נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נַעֲבֹר֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם
דֶּ֧רֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נֵלֵ֗ךְ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֔אול
t: נְעִבַּר כְּעַן בְּאַרְעָךְ לָא נְעִבַּר בַּחֲקַל וּבִכְרַם
בְּאֹרַח מַלְכָּא נֵזֵל לָא נִסְטֵי לְיַמִּינָא וְלִשְׂמָאלָא
e: Please let us pass through your land, we will not pass through any field or vineyard,
and we will not drink well water;
we will travel by the king’s road, we will not turn aside to the right or left,
until we have passed through your territory.”
Edom responded,
“You shall not pass through me (my land) [my border],
lest I go out against you [to kill you] with the sword!”

t: וַאֲמָרוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֹרַח כְּבִישָׁא נִסַּק
e: Bnei Yisroel said, “We will go up by the [paved] highway,
and if we or our cattle drink your water
we will pay for it,
it is just nothing, we only want [with no evil intent] to pass through on foot.”
Then (Edom) responded, “Do not pass through!”
Edom came to confront [Bnei Yisroel]
with a massive number of people [an army] and a strong hand.

h: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן אֱד֗וֹם נְתֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֲבֹ֖ר בִּגְבֻל֑וֹ
t: וְסָרֵיב אֱדוֹמָאָה לְמִשְׁבַק יָת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמֶעֱבַּר בִּתְחוּמֵיהּ
e: Edom refused to allow Yisroel to pass through its territory,
and Yisroel turned aside from him.

t: וַאֲתוֹ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּל כְּנִשְׁתָּא לְהֹר טוּרָא:
e: They traveled from Kodeish,
and the entire community of Bnei Yisroel came to Mount Hor.

h: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן בְּהֹ֣ר הָהָ֑ר
t: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְמשֶׁה וּלְאַהֲרֹן בְּהֹר טוּרָא עַל
e: Adonoy spoke to Moshe and Aharon at Mount Hor,
at the border of the land of Edom, saying.

t: עַל דִּי סָרִיבְתּוּן עַל מֵימְרִי לְמֵי מַצּוּתָא:
e: “Aharon will now be gathered (die) to his people,
for he shall not enter the land
that I have given to Bnei Yisroel,
because you defied My word at the waters of dispute.
Take Aharon
and his son Elozor,
and bring them up to Mount Hor.
Remove Aharon’s vestments
and dress his son Elozor in them;
Aharon will be gathered in and die there.”
Moshe did
as Adonoy commanded;
and they went up Mount Hor
in the presence of the entire community.

h: וַיַּפְשֵׁט֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתָם֙ אֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֣ר בְּנ֔וֹ
t: וְאַשְׁלַח משֶׁה יָת אַהֲרֹן יָת לְבוּשׁוֹהִי וְאַלְבֵּישׁ יָתְהוֹן יָת אֶלְעָזָר בְּרֵיהּ
e: Moshe then removed Aharon’s vestments and dressed Aharon’s son, Elozor, in them;
Aharon died there on top of the mountain,
and Moshe and Elozor descended from the mountain.
The entire community saw
that Aharon died;
and they wept for Aharon thirty days,
the entire house of Yisroel.

t: וּשְׁמַע כְּנַעֲנָאָה מַלְכָּא דַעֲרָד יָתֵב דָּרוֹמָא
e: The Canaanite King of Arad heard — who lived in the south — that
Yisroel had come
by the route of the spies;
he attacked [waged war with] Yisroel,
and he took from them a captive.

t: אִם מִמְסַר תִּמְסַר יָת עַמָּא הָדֵין בִּידִי
e: Yisroel made a vow to [before] Adonoy and said,
“If You will deliver this people into my hand,
I shall consecrate their cities.”

h: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י
t: וְקַבֵּיל יְיָ צְלוֹתֵיהּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְסַר יָת כְּנַעֲנָאָה
e: Adonoy heard Yisroel’s voice [prayers], and He delivered the Canaanites (into Yisroel’s hand),
and he (Yisroel) destroyed them and [consecrated] their cities;
the region was named Chormo.

t: וּנְטָלוּ מֵהֹר טוּרָא אֹרַח יַמָּא דְסוּף
e: They then traveled from Mount Hor by the Reed Sea route,
in order to circle around the land of Edom;
traveling was insufferable to the [soul of the] people.
The people spoke out [complained] against [the word of] God and [they fought] Moshe,
“Why did you bring us up out of Egypt
to die in the wilderness?
There is no food and no water,
and we are disgusted
with this rotten bread [which is eaten simply].”

h: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים
t: וְגָרֵי יְיָ בְּעַמָּא יָת חִיוַן קָלָן
e: Adonoy sent against the people the consuming snakes,
and they bit the people,
and many people of Yisroel died.

h: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי־דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ
t: וַאֲתָא עַמָּא לְמשֶׁה וַאֲמָרוּ חַבְנָא אֲרֵי אִתְרַעַמְנָא קֳדָם יְיָ וְעִמָּךְ נְצֵינָא
e: The people came to Moshe and said, “We have sinned by speaking against [complaining before] Adonoy and [fighting with] you;
pray to [before] Adonoy
that He remove the snakes from us.”
Moshe prayed on behalf of the people.

h: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף
t: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְמשֶׁה עֲבֵיד לָךְ קָלְיָא
e: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Make yourself [the image of] a consuming snake,
and place it upon a banner;
and anyone bitten will
look at it and live.”

t: וַהֲוָה כַּד נָכִית חִוְיָא יָת גַּבְרָא
e: Moshe made a copper snake
and placed it on the banner;
whenever a snake bit a person,
he would gaze upon the copper snake and live.
Bnei Yisroel traveled on
and camped in Ovos.

h: וַֽיַּחֲנ֞וּ בְּעִיֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבָרִ֗ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב
t: וּשְׁרוֹ בִּמְגִיזַת עֲבָרָאֵי בְּמַדְבְּרָא דִּי עַל אַפֵּי מוֹאָב
e: They traveled from Ovos
and camped in the wasteland passes in the wilderness, facing Moav,
eastward of the sun.
They traveled from there
and camped in the valley of Zered.
They traveled from there
and camped opposite Arnon, in the wilderness,
extending from the Emorite border;
Arnon being the Moav border
between Moav and the Emorite.
Concerning this will be told in the
Book of the Wars of Adonoy,
“He gave at the Reeds (Sea)
and [the might at] the valleys of Arnon.
And the spillage in the valleys
when it turned to dwell at Ar,
and then leaned on the border of Moav.

h: הִ֣וא הַבְּאֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה
t: הִיא בֵירָא דִּי אֲמַר יְיָ לְמשֶׁה
e: From there, to the well;
this is the well of which Adonoy said to Moshe,
‘Gather the people
and I will give them water.’”
It was then that Yisroel sang
this song [of praise]:
“Arise, O well, sing to it!

h: בְּאֵ֞ר חֲפָר֣וּהָ שָׂרִ֗ים כָּר֙וּהָ֙ נְדִיבֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם
t: בֵּירָא דְּחָפְרוּהָ רַבְרְבַיָּא כְּרוּהָ רֵישֵׁי עַמָּא
e: The well dug by princes, that the nobles of the nation excavated,
through the lawgiver, with their staffs;
from the wilderness a gift [was given to them].
The gift [given to them] (traveled) to the valley,
and from the valley [rose with them] to the heights.
And from the heights to the valley that is in the field of Moav,
at the top of the peak
that overlooks the wastelands.”
Yisroel sent emissaries
to Sichon, King of the Emorite, saying.

h: אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם
t: אֲעִבַר בְּאַרְעָךְ לָא נִסְטֵי בַּחֲקַל וּבִכְרַם
e: “Let me pass through your land, we will not turn aside into the fields and vineyards,
we will not drink well water;
we will go by the King’s road
until we have passed through your territory.”

h: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף סִיחֹ֜ן אֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֗וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֞א לִקְרַ֤את יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּדְבָּ֔רָה
t: וְלָא שְׁבַק סִיחוֹן יָת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמֶעְבַּר בִּתְחוּמֵיהּ
וּכְנַשׁ סִיחוֹן יָת כָּל עַמֵּיהּ וּנְפַק לָקֳדָמוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַדְבְּרָא
e: But Sichon did not allow Yisroel to pass through his territory;
Sichon gathered all his people and went out against Yisroel to the wilderness;
he came to Yohatz
and attacked [waged war with] Yisroel.

h: וַיִּירַ֨שׁ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ מֵֽאַרְנֹ֗ן עַד־יַבֹּק֙ עַד־בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן
t: וִירֵת יָת אַרְעֵיהּ מֵאַרְנוֹנָא עַד יוּבְקָא עַד בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן
e: Yisroel defeated him with the edge of the sword
and took possession of his land; from Arnon to the Yabok, as far as Amon[’s border],
because Amon’s border was impregnable.
Yisroel took [captured]
all these cities;
Yisroel settled in all the cities of the Emorite,
in Cheshbon and all its daughters [villages].

t: וְהוּא אַגַּח קְרָבָא בְּמַלְכָּא דְמוֹאָב קַדְמָאָה
וּנְסִיב יָת כָּל אַרְעֵיהּ מִידֵיהּ עַד אַרְנוֹן:
e: For Cheshbon was
then a city of Sichon, King of the Emorites,
and he had waged war against the first king of Moav,
and took all his land from his hand, as far as Arnon.

t: עַל כֵּן יֵימְרוּן מְתָלַיָּא עוּלוּ לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן
e: Concerning this, the parable tellers say: “Come to Cheshbon,
may it be built and established as the city of Sichon.
For [an Easterly wind as strong as] a fire went forth from Cheshbon,
[waged war as] a flame from Sichon’s capital;
it consumed [killing the nation that dwelled in] Ar [Lechoyas], of Moav,
[killing] the masters [priests who serve in the house of idol worship] of Arnon’s heights.
Woe to you, O Moav,
you are destroyed, people of [who serve] Kemosh,
he rendered your sons as refugees, and your daughters captives,
of Sichon, King of Emori.
Their kingdom was uprooted from Cheshbon as far as Divon [whose reign has ended];
we made them desolate as far as Nofach
near Meidva.”
Yisroel settled
in the land of the Emorite.
Moshe sent [men] to spy on Ya’zer,
and they captured its surrounding villages,
and drove out the Emorites that were there.

h: וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתָ֜ם ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃
t: וּנְפַק עוֹג מַלְכָּא דְמַתְנָן לָקֳדָמוּתְהוֹן הוּא וְכָל עַמֵּיהּ לְאַגָּחָא קְרָבָא לְאֶדְרֶעִי:
e: They then turned
and headed toward the Bashan [Masnon];
and Og, King of the Bashan [Masnon], came out against them he with all his people, to wage war at Edre’i.

h: כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ
t: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְמשֶׁה לָא תִדְחַל מִנֵּיהּ
אֲרֵי בִידָךְ מְסָרִית יָתֵיהּ וְיָת כָּל עַמֵּיהּ וְיָת אַרְעֵיהּ
כְּמָא דִי עֲבַדְתְּ לְסִיחוֹן מַלְכָּא דֶאֱמוֹרָאָה
e: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Do not be afraid of him,
for into your hand I have delivered Ihim and all his people and territory;
do to him
as you have done to Sichon, King of the Emorite,
who lives in Cheshbon.”

t: וּמְחוֹ יָתֵיהּ וְיָת בְּנוֹהִי וְיָת כָּל עַמֵּיהּ
e: And they killed him (Og), his sons, and all his people,
leaving no survivors;
and they took possession of his land.
Bnei Yisroel traveled
and camped in the western plains of Moav,
across the Yardein from Yereicho.
